title: Enforce key-location awareness and attribute-driven access controls for KMS-backed objects
author: Liam Chen
release_notes: Add KMS key-location routing and attribute-driven RBAC checks; migration tool included to backfill key metadata. No user-facing API changes; operators must run migration and enable feature flag.
description: Motivation: customers require stronger guarantees that keys and encrypted artifacts are served from approved geographic locations and that access decisions consider dynamic request attributes. This PR implements a KMS routing layer that is key-location aware and couples it with RBAC v2 policy predicates based on resource attributes and key residency. Summary of changes: 1) new kms-router module that resolves key metadata and routes encryption/decryption requests to region-appropriate backends; 2) RBAC v2 policy predicates and policy-to-key binding rules that allow policy authors to express allow/deny based on key.residency and request.attributes; 3) audit enrichment to include resolved key_location and policy_decision in every KMS audit event; 4) migration tool to backfill key metadata for existing keys and mark provenance; 5) console UI to display key residency and a flag to opt into strict routing; 6) config flag and gradual rollout behavior for Dedicated and Private deployments. Backwards compatibility: default behavior preserves current routing for customers who do not enable the feature flag; policies that do not reference key attributes remain unchanged. Security review: design reviewed by SEC-88; threat model updated to include cross-region fallback and key-provenance mismatch detection. Testing: unit + integration tests included, and a small chaos job in perf-canary to validate fallback rates. Rollout plan: stage behind feature flag, enable for internal infra on 2025-12-05, enable self-serve for EU customers first, monitor audit logs and SLOs, then widen scope. Operator steps: run tools/migrations/kms_keymeta_migration with --dry-run, verify sample backfill, then run without dry-run; set config.feature.enable_kms_location_routing=true; update Dedicated autoscaler policy to prefer region-local pools. Checklist: [x] design doc linked ENG-2719 [x] unit tests [x] integration tests [x] migration tool [x] docs updated [x] console UX [x] security review

changes_snippet: func ResolveKeyLocation(keyID string) (string, error) { meta, err := resolver.Lookup(keyID); if err != nil { return "", err } return meta.Location, nil } // RBAC predicate: key.location == request.attr['region']
review_thread: Maya Singh (review): Please add a unit test covering policy evaluation when key metadata is missing. Also call out audit fields in the docs.
Author (Liam Chen): Added integration tests and documentation; migration tool marks provenance to avoid ambigous backfills.
Ethan Brooks (review): Concern about fallback behavior causing silent cross-region decrypts; recommend an explicit deny-by-default policy during rollout.
Author: Implemented a config flag that toggles strict-routing; added a metric `kms.routing.fallback_count` and an alert to SRE.
Carlos Rivera (LGTM): Verified migration on a staging snapshot; audit events include key_location and decision_id.
Maya Singh: Approved after test expansions.
migration_instructions: Run tools/migrations/kms_keymeta_migration --target=production --concurrency=8; verify sample keys with tools/kms_cli lookup; enable config.feature.enable_kms_location_routing in a single region; monitor kms.routing.fallback_count and audit logs for unexpected decisions; when stable, flip strict-routing flag and roll out to other regions.
notes: This PR intentionally avoids forcing a tenant-level KMS scoping change; the model is opt-in and supports gradual enforcement. Operators with air-gapped deployments must run the migration tool locally to populate key metadata.
